newsitem.title: CHINA: China securities watchdog re-licences brokerages.
newsitem.headline: China securities watchdog re-licences brokerages.

text.p: China's securities authorities have begun a re-registration of all local and foreign brokerages wishing to trade foreign currency B and H shares, the China Securities newspaper said on Thursday.

Major local brokerages have long traded the shares, but last November the authorities issued new rules governing the trading of B shares listed on China's two stock exchanges and China shares listed in Hong Kong and on other overseas exchanges.
Based on the re-registration applications, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) will give qualified brokerages licences to conduct the business, the newspaper said.

The rules require domestic securities houses and trust and investment companies to have a minimum of 50 million yuan in net assets or securities capital before they are eligible to trade foreign currency China shares.
Foreign brokerages must be investment banks, securities houses or other financial organisations allowed to do securities business in accordance with the laws and regulations of their home countries.

The rules also require a brokerage to have at least 80 million yuan or its equivalent in assets to be eligible to underwrite share issues, and at least 120 million yuan or its equivalent in assets to be the lead underwriter or chief international coordinator.
